newResearchLeads.title: Winter (The Flood)
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Louvre INV 7306/MR2336, 1660–64; exact Genesis Flood disaster subject as allegorical Winter. Depicts survivors amid rising flood, NOT Noah covenant; museum source verified, no physical master acquired.

newResearchLeads.title: Joseph pardons his Brothers
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: National Gallery NG1219 (probably 1515), original oil-on-wood horizontal 36.2 x 141.6 cm continuous narrative culminating in forgiveness Genesis 45; historical source but unfit narrow hero crop.

newResearchLeads.title: The Crossing of the Red Sea
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: NGV 1843-4 original Poussin painting; Exodus 14 scene is AFTER the Red Sea has closed over Egyptians, not the initial water parting. Original source exact, already in research; no duplicate source acquisition or artwork record.

newResearchLeads.title: The Adoration of the Golden Calf
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: National Gallery London NG5597 original Poussin painting Exodus 32 dancing at Golden Calf and smashing tablets; companion to NGV Red Sea. Full-width OT anchor; source existing, rights and crop unresolved.

newResearchLeads.title: Résurrection du fils de la veuve de Naïm
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Louvre official record for a related Simon Vouet study explicitly states the oil painting, by Eustache Le Sueur, is preserved at Saint-Roch church in Paris. Drawing itself not exact whole painting; obtain object/image and rights before ranking.

newResearchLeads.title: Christ Asleep during the Tempest
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: exact storm narrative; moment before Christ calms the sea

newResearchLeads.title: Saint Peter Walking on the Water
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: NGA signed 1525 engraving; accurate Christ/Peter in water and boat. The NGA oil Christ at Sea of Galilee (object 41637) is NOT Matthew 14 but John 21, so exclude that painting from Walking on Water.

newResearchLeads.title: The Transfiguration
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: exact Gospel subject; collection details retained at heritage source

newResearchLeads.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Exactly the return/reconciliation episode Luke 15:20–24, not entire parable. Source institutional UK Hermitage Foundation; 2020 image photograph credited to State Hermitage and reproduction rights HELD. Large painterly masterpiece, full composition check needed.

newResearchLeads.title: The Four Elements: Fire
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Martha and Mary with Christ appear as a small background scene

newResearchLeads.title: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: National Gallery NG1375 exact Luke 10:38–42 appears as SMALL BACKGROUND vignette in kitchen genre painting; remarkable quality but narratively weak mobile crop. Do not label foreground kitchen women the historical sisters automatically. Reproduction image rights pending.

newResearchLeads.title: Handing over of the Keys
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Vatican Museums explicitly tie Sistine Chapel fresco to Matthew 16:13-20. Exact Petrine primacy scene (keys). Large landscape chapel fresco, principal figures small on phone and Vatican photograph rights separate.

newResearchLeads.title: The Incredulity of St Thomas
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Rijksmuseum SK-A-1965, c.1626–30, exact John 20:24–29 encounter in Baroque oil, public domain. Museum reports substantial surface abrasion, losses, discolored varnish; technical colour/quality check before artistic promotion. No Caravaggio attribution.

newResearchLeads.title: Christ on the Road to Emmaus
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: NGA museum object records three figures walking along road; genuinely represents Luke 24 initial road event unlike the already researched Velázquez/Piazzetta supper scenes. Artistic quality versus masterpieces needs human comparison, no automatic replacement.

newResearchLeads.title: Christ's Charge to Peter
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: V&A Royal Loans.3 painted tapestry cartoon c.1515–16, exact Risen Christ commissioning Peter John 21:15–17 with sheep and Peter. NOT standard oil canvas. Royal Collection Trust reproduction rights and format held; extraordinary relevance for biblical doctrine, full image and textile-cartoon category required.

newResearchLeads.title: The Washing of the Feet
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Prado inventory P002824 autograph Tintoretto, 1548–49. Exact John 13:1–17 washing scene, but enormous 210×533cm panorama with Christ/Peter at far right: strong museum painting unsuitable for centered phone hero. Prado reproduction rights held.

newResearchLeads.title: Saints Peter and John Healing the Lame Man
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Met object 437330, 1655 oil on canvas, exact Acts 3:1–10 and temple step composition, public-domain object with Met Open Access. Prefer source-exact Poussin over inaccurate generic Acts illustration; final full-quality and crop checks pending.

newResearchLeads.title: The Baptism of the Eunuch
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Rijksmuseum RP-P-1961-1043 describes Philip baptizing Ethiopian royal official; exact event, but print not oil painting. Caption Philip the evangelist/deacon, not Apostle Philip.

newResearchLeads.title: The Raising of Tabitha
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: National Gallery London inventory NG4573 (possibly c.1540), says probably Peter raising Tabitha; damaged/extended edges, paint alteration and later reconstructed head. Visually appealing but preservation fidelity and attribution warning are essential.

newResearchLeads.artist: Philip Galle after Jan van der Straet
newResearchLeads.title: Cornelius Worshipping Saint Peter
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: NGA 54321 engraving of Cornelius kneeling before Peter. One moment of Acts 10, not automatically depiction of the baptism or full conversion. A map/context and text may suffice.

newResearchLeads.title: Paul and Barnabas at Lystra
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Met 1971.255, Jacob Pynas original oil on wood 48.3x73.3 cm, Acts 14:8-18 scene at Lystra. Institutional public-domain source, higher artistic potential than a generic print. Do not confuse with Jordaens chalk drawing 335629 or Guerra's AFTER-STONING Acts 14:20 scene 339081.

newResearchLeads.artist: Flemish workshop after Raphael and his workshop
newResearchLeads.title: Saint Paul Preaching at Athens
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: Official Vatican Museums source documents 1515-1521 Acts tapestry from Raphael/workshop preparatory cartoons, Acts 17:16-34 Paul before Areopagus, now on display in 2026 in the Papal Palace Castel Gandolfo. A tapestry, NOT directly an oil Raphael canvas; rights/reproduction and large size hold. Strong exact scene and major historical art.

newResearchLeads.title: Saint Paul Shipwrecked on the Island of Malta
newResearchLeads.matchNotes: NGA 90938 signed 1634 print depicts shipwreck near coast, survivors and wrecked ship. Existing Acts route map is more useful for geographical context; print optional.
